title: Find out whether Position and Size takes numbers on a piece inside a copy
goal: A piece inside a copy of a component owns nothing: its size, its place and its look are refilled from the original after every edit. The canvas knows this and offers such a piece no handles. It is not clear whether the Position and Size panel knows it too, or whether it offers X, Y, W, H and A as typeable numbers that the next sync quietly puts back. Somebody typing into a box and watching it spring back with nothing said would read that as a broken panel.
notes:
Not reproduced. Noticed on 2026-09-09 while adding the angle field: Sources/Photonz/CanvasGroups.swift offersOwnHandles excludes a component piece (componentPiece(of:) != nil), but Sources/PhotonzCore/LayerGeometry.swift LayerGeometryEditing takes only the layer and its container and has no idea about components, so nothing in it can refuse on those grounds. I did not get as far as selecting a piece inside a copy in the probe to watch it happen, so this is an open question rather than a bug. To check: Scripts/probe-app.sh, drop a Button from the Library, step into the copy, pick the label inside it, type an X and watch.

ANSWERED 2026-09-12. The panel already refuses, so there is nothing to do.

What it does today: with a piece inside a copy picked, Position & Size is not on the panel at all. InspectorPanel.swift:791 subtracts it, with colour, effects, type, layout and arrange, in sectionsAPieceDoesNotOwn: 'A piece INSIDE a copy owns nothing.' The only section left is Component, which names the piece and its original and offers Select Copy, Edit Original and Detach. Watched in the probe, five expect claims, screenshot piecegeo-8-no-numbers-for-a-piece-sc.png.

The original note was right that LayerGeometryEditing has no idea about components: over a piece it returns canMove=true canSetWidth=true canRotate=true with fixedReason nil on every field, and writing x=999 onto that piece then syncing restores x=20. It simply never gets asked, because the section is gone before it would be. That is the right height for the refusal: a piece owns none of its colour, type or effects either, and five dead boxes with a sentence under each would say the same thing five times. LayerGeometryEditing's doc comment now says so.

The note also assumed you reach a piece by stepping into a copy on the canvas. You cannot: Document.hitTestPath folds a copy's contents into the copy (Document.swift:332) and Layer.isOpenableGroup is false for a copy (ComponentInstances.swift:33), so a click, a double click, a band and the Layers list all land on the whole copy. The route that DOES put a piece in the selection is Library > Styles > Select What Uses This, because a piece carries its original's style bindings.

Walks: Scripts/playtest/piece-geometry-walk.json (the routes, and the panel over a piece), Scripts/playtest/style-users-walk.json (the style route). Tests: ComponentPieceEditingTests aClickOnAPiecePicksTheWholeCopy, aDoubleClickCannotStepIntoACopy, theLayersListNeverOpensACopy.
acceptance: There is a plain answer, written into this task, about what the panel does today when a piece inside a copy is selected
If the panel does take numbers that get put back, the fields read as numbers worked out for you, with a sentence saying the original decides them
If the panel already refuses them, the task is closed as nothing to do and says so

log.note: Reproduced both halves. In PhotonzCore: LayerGeometryEditing(layer:in:) over a piece inside a copy returns canMove=true, canSetWidth=true, canRotate=true and no reason on any of them, and writing x=999 onto that piece then calling syncComponentInstances() puts it back to 20. So the type really would offer numbers it could never keep.

Correction to the entry above: LayerGeometryEditing would indeed offer all five, but the refusal is made a level up. InspectorPanel.swift:791 subtracts Position & Size from the sections a picked piece is offered, alongside colour, effects, type and layout (sectionsAPieceDoesNotOwn). With a piece picked the panel shows ONE section, Component, reading 'Rectangle is part of a copy. What it shows comes from the original, so it is set with the knobs below', with Select Copy, Edit Original and Detach under it. No X, Y, W, H or A anywhere.

Watched in the probe. Scripts/playtest/piece-geometry-walk.json: a click on a piece, the double click that steps into any other group, a band and the Layers list all pick the whole copy (four expectPicked claims); then a piece is made the selection outright and five expect claims read X, Y, W, H and A as absent. Screenshot piecegeo-8-no-numbers-for-a-piece-sc.png.

Also found and reproduced the one route that DOES put a piece in the selection, which the original note assumed was a click: Library > Styles > Select What Uses This. A piece carries its original's colour and effect style bindings, so the button picks the original's layers and every copy's pieces together. Pinned in Scripts/playtest/style-users-walk.json (style says '4 colors', four layers picked, Position & Size present because the section only goes away when a piece is picked ON ITS OWN). Typing 900 into X there moved the original and the copy followed it, so nothing on screen ended up saying two different things.

Closed as nothing to do on the panel. Shipped the evidence so the answer does not have to be found again: two walks, three tests in ComponentPieceEditingTests pinning that no gesture reaches a piece, a corrected note on LayerGeometryEditing saying where the refusal actually lives, and a playtestControl tag on Select What Uses This so a walk can press it. Filed one p2 follow-up about the Layers list saying 4 layers selected while only two of them have rows. No audit: nothing new to try in the app.
